WIC27A-01.explanation: With traffic gone and nothing else changed (the mill's orders kept, the same families at the counters, no building newer than 1951), the expressway left the town held in its 1958 form: it "fossilized" it. "Drained" fails because the mill kept its orders and the families kept their stores; only through traffic left. "Engulfed" and "fragmented" both fail because the road ran across the river with its nearest exit nine miles off, so the city's spread could not reach the town and the road cut through none of it.

WIC27A-02.explanation: Losing their advertisers cost the papers two thirds of their pages, every outside bureau and most of their wire service, so they could no longer cover what they once had: radio "hamstrung" them. "Dethroned" fails because radio read the papers' stories only after the papers were out, so print still told the news first. "Homogenized" fails because the pages left went to each city's own courts and council. "Fractured" fails because the papers voted together on cutting the wire service.

WIC27A-03.explanation: Coal brought in each summer was kept behind the quay and drawn on all year by the cities' steamships on every voyage, so the island was their "depot." "Haven" fails because the steamships called on every voyage because their fuel was there, not to escape storms. "Gateway" fails because sailing ships went straight through without stopping. "Fortress" fails because the island's people were dockworkers handling coal.

WIC27A-04.explanation: The founders met there nightly, couriers to the cells at home left from it, and the movement's mail and files were kept there, so the café was where the movement was run: its "headquarters." "Hub" fails because the founders met only after the café had closed, when its ordinary crowd of exiles had gone. "Embassy" fails because the room was kept so secret that even the police never learned its use, so it spoke for the movement to no outsider. "Hothouse" fails because the men at the table were the movement's founders, not newcomers being formed.

WIC27A-05.explanation: Salmon tagged in the pool beside the log turn up weeks later on gravel beds miles upstream, so the log's pool is a resting stop on their journey: the valley's "hostel." "Hatchery" fails because the salmon spawn on those gravel beds upstream, not at the log. "Highway" fails because the log lies along the current, parallel to the banks, joining neither. "Garden" fails because the winter flood runs over the trunk and takes each year's seedlings.

WIC27A-06.explanation: Barred from enrolling new men, the union could only shrink as its veterans retired, until its last local sold the hall in 1931, so the ruling set it on a sure road to its end: it "doomed" the union. "Disbanded" fails because the union lasted thirty-seven more years. "Defanged" fails because employers paid every man the union scale rather than risk a walkout. "Divided" fails because the veterans remained a single body that employers feared would walk out together.

WIC27A-07.explanation: Every line had been reworked for effect (the tricks put in rising order, a rhyming riddle, the surprise moved to the last line), so retelling had "honed" the tale. "Distilled" and "fused" fail because a telling still took as long as reading the printed text, so the tale had neither been cut down nor joined to other material. "Domesticated" fails because the riddle rhymed on the names of the desert's wells, so the tale was still set in the desert.

WIC27A-08.explanation: One coastal family owned every palm and well, and its stewards had tenants pick the dates and carry them to its own warehouses, so the oasis was a single owner's holding worked for profit: an "estate." "Emporium" fails because the whole crop went to the family's warehouses on the coast, so nothing was sold at the oasis. "Fairground" fails because the autumn crowd was the family's tenants at work. "Gatehouse" fails because caravans watered free.

WIC27B-01.explanation: Stoats born in the eastern wood settled in the western one, passing through the hedge from end to end in a single night, so it was their "lane." "Inn" fails because a stoat logged at both ends on the same night did not stop there to rest. "Lair" fails because these stoats were born in one wood and settled in the other. "Larder" fails because the passing stoats took nothing from the bank's voles.

WIC27B-02.explanation: The flood filled channels, ditches and hollows with sand, and the next spring farmers plowed whole farms in straight furrows, so it "leveled" their fields. "Irrigated" fails because rain returned that winter, so the flood's water gave the crop nothing the rain did not. "Nourished" fails because wheat on the new sand grew no thicker than elsewhere. "Marooned" fails because the sand filled the old channels and the farmers plowed every part of their farms.

WIC27B-03.explanation: Behind a sealed wall, adults and children were laid in layers over three thousand years, their bones uncut and an antler across each layer, while the living cooked and ate in the camps by the river, so the cave was the hunters' "mortuary." "Lookout" fails because the ledge was walled shut, so no one could see out from it. "Icebox" fails because the reindeer parts on the ledge are antlers laid over human bones, while the butchered meat bones lie in the camps. "Lodge" fails because the hearths of those centuries lie in the riverside camps.

WIC27B-04.explanation: A naval shipyard paid him load by load, and afterward he hired men to pull stumps and sow grass, so he had sold the oaks: he had "logged" the estate. "Mortgaged" fails because money paid load by load by a shipyard is a buyer's price, not a loan. "Leased" fails because he himself paid the men who worked the land. "Liquidated" fails because he went on paying the estate's hands until 1858.

WIC27B-05.explanation: Infected snails stayed small and slow but kept breeding and lived as long as the rest, so the worm drew on them steadily without killing them: it "milked" its host. "Neutered" fails because infected snails still laid eggs every week. "Manipulated" fails because infected snails stayed in the shaded weed bases with the others, away from the tips where ducks feed. "Immunized" fails because the bacterium took both kinds in proportion to their numbers.

WIC27B-06.explanation: Its layers come one a year, all alike, and scientists whose own lakes held the rainfall records set the dates of those records against its count, so the lake was the region's "metronome." "Ledger" fails because layers the same whatever the weather record nothing about any year, and the rainfall records were the other lakes'. "Microcosm" fails because scientists studied the other lakes directly and only borrowed this one's count. "Museum" fails because what others took from it was a count of years, a measure of time, not anything old kept to be seen.

WIC27B-07.explanation: The older company's spare parts fitted the newcomer's cheaper machine throughout, and its engineers had worked from machines bought in shops, so the newcomer had "mimicked" its rival. "Infiltrated" fails because the design came from machines anyone could buy, not from inside the older firm. "Leapfrogged" fails because a machine that takes the rival's parts throughout is no step beyond it. "Isolated" fails because dealers stocked both machines side by side.

WIC27B-08.explanation: Silver bearing twelve owners' marks, from the ports a crew of twelve traded at, sat in one pot in the shed they shared, so the hoard was money they had pooled: its owners' "kitty." "Insurance" fails because twelve owners' marks show many contributors, not one household's reserve. "Loot" fails because the silver carried the marks of the crew who owned it and came from the ports where they traded. "Inventory" fails because marked shares of money held in common are not a craftsman's stock.

WIC27C-01.explanation: Outside strains were grown beside the usual wheat for five seasons and farmers adopted only the ones that held up, so the station was where new wheat was tried first: a "testbed." "Wellspring" fails because the strains were bred in other states; the station sorted them but originated nothing. "Yardstick" fails because the fixed standard in the strips was the district's usual wheat, while the station's own plantings changed with every batch. "Stopgap" fails because the trials ran every spring for forty years, a standing program rather than cover for the closed merchant until trade returned.

WIC27C-02.explanation: The city's merchants and boats moved to the village quay while the same city shops kept getting their fish by cart, so the rule "uprooted" the market: the whole market went on, in another place. "Stifled" fails because the city's shops were supplied as before, so the city's fish market lost its site, not its trade. "Saturated" fails because the boats landed at the village, so no fish reached the city's quay to glut it. "Steadied" fails because a market whose merchants, boats and quay all moved within two years was overturned, not settled.

WIC27C-03.explanation: Bare rock grooved downhill where farms and houses stood, with their beams now in the sea, shows that the eruption dragged the surface off: it "scoured" the island. "Smothered" fails because the rock was left bare, with nothing lying over it. "Submerged" fails because the tide still reaches the old mark in the quay's bedrock, so the beams were carried into the sea while the land stayed up. "Tilted" fails because the stream still runs down its old gully, which tipped ground would have turned aside.

WIC27C-04.explanation: Water seeps through the lake's limestone floor into caverns that empty into another valley, so the river loses half its water there: the lake is a "sink." "Valve" fails because the water missing in dry summers is not held for later; it comes out as springs in another valley. "Tributary" fails because the river leaves the lake half as wide. "Thermostat" fails because the seepage keeps the lake shallow, and the ponds must turn to wells in August.

WIC27C-05.explanation: The oak was shaved away from behind the paint and the altarpiece's back is now canvas on aluminum, so the restorers "transferred" it to a new support. "Stabilized" fails because the oak was sound; it was removed to save weight for a tour, not to arrest any decay. "Scrubbed" fails because the saints were still smoke-browned, so nothing was cleaned. "Uncovered" fails because the crowds saw the same saints they had always known, so nothing hidden came into view.

WIC27C-06.explanation: Icy bodies passing near the giant were flung onto stretched paths, most out of the system, so the giant acted as the system's "slingshot." "Umbrella" fails because a quarter of the flung bodies were sent inward across the rocky planets' orbits, so the giant aimed bodies at the inner planets rather than shielding them. "Shepherd" fails because the belt lost half its bodies instead of being kept in bounds. "Tether" fails because the bodies near the giant left on long paths rather than being held in place.

WIC27C-07.explanation: A three-minute side held only the first few verses, and the young learned only those, so the records "stripped" the ballads of most of their verses. "Smoothed" fails because the engineers took each fiddle and voice as they found it in farmhouse kitchens. "Transplanted" fails because the records sold in the region's own mountain towns, so the songs stayed where they were. "Silenced" fails because the young people sang the songs at every weekend dance.

WIC27C-08.explanation: The sheds took in thousands of imported cars and parts that dealers drew on as orders came, so the plant was the company's "warehouse." "Toehold" fails because the company had sold cars in the country since 1930, so the plant took over an established trade rather than opening one. "Schoolhouse" fails because its workers spent their days washing, checking and loading finished cars, so it taught no one to build them. "Showroom" fails because sheds holding up to twenty thousand cars are built for stock, not for visitors.

WIC27D-01.explanation: The crest lies dry from the shore to the island at low tide, and the town's sheep spend each summer on the island, so the bar is the town's "causeway" to its pasture. "Breakwater" fails because the fleet still winters on the beach like boats on the open coast. "Barricade" fails because eight feet of water covers the bar at high tide. "Chokepoint" fails because the fleet can cross anywhere along the bar.

WIC27D-02.explanation: The gale stripped the crest's sand down to a bed of cobbles, and afterward the spit wore away more slowly than ever before, so the gale had "armored" it. "Cleaved" fails because the keeper's cart still ran along the crest to town. "Blunted" fails because boats still moored behind the hook. "Broadened" fails because the lagoon-side boathouses still stood at the water's edge.

WIC27D-03.explanation: The city's wells were too brackish to drink, the canal brought spring water from the hills, and pipes carried that water to fountains across the city, so it was the city's "aqueduct." "Artery" fails because two feet of water floats no barge. "Commons" fails because its banks are hedged and fenced off. "Border" fails because its water feeds the city's parishes on both sides, so the city lies on both banks.

WIC27D-04.explanation: The council bought at harvest prices and sold to whichever port paid most, and the city needed a hearth tax only in the two years war stopped the shipments, so the granary's trade paid the city's way: it was the city's "coffer." "Ballast" fails because the grain was shipped downriver and never reached the city's own market. "Backstop" fails because it was shipped out even in famine years. "Cudgel" fails because the council bought from every village alike, quarrel or no quarrel, and sold on price alone.

WIC27D-05.explanation: Galleries under sixty feet of chalk were kept lit and stocked through the war, and the square emptied within minutes whenever the sirens sounded, so the quarry was the town's "bunker." "Bazaar" and "arena" fail because a pond covers the floor, leaving no ground for stalls or a show. "Cesspool" fails because the pond is clear enough for boys to fish.

WIC27D-06.explanation: Gravel shallows reach the island from both banks, and the harvest carts get to the market town on the far bank by way of it, so it is the valley's "crossing." "Anchorage" fails because the current runs fastest over those shallows, so no barge can lie there. "Citadel" fails because raiders burned the island's barns with everyone else's. "Ark" fails because spring floods leave driftwood across its crown.

WIC27D-07.explanation: Drips collect in a clay-floored basin that fills over the winter and sinks over the summer, and the village draws on it in dry years, so the cave is the hill's "cistern." "Chimney" fails because every passage ends in clay. "Bellows" fails because a candle flame stands upright in all weathers. "Cooler" fails because ferns stay green inside the mouth all winter.

WIC27D-08.explanation: The glaze stopped letting light through and dimmed the brushwork while the white ground looked whiter, so it had turned pale and opaque: the firing had "clouded" it. "Blackened" fails because the bowls looked whiter, not darker. "Blistered" fails because the glaze was as smooth as glass. "Cracked" fails because tea washed out without a trace.

WIC27E-01.explanation: Clear water stood for nine days on salt-crusted fields and drained down through sandy ground, after which the same wheat grew as well as on the upper slopes, so the flood "rinsed" the salt out of the lower fields. "Reseeded" fails because the fallow strips fed the cattle no better than usual. "Replenished" fails because clear snowmelt adds no silt, and "plowed" fails because the old stubble was still there to graze.

WIC27E-02.explanation: A hill lord built the temple with monks of another order, set its festival for the city's own spring week, and within ten years the city's festival tolls had fallen by half, so it was the city temple's "rival". "Offshoot" fails because its monks came from a coastal order with its own rule. "Replica" fails because its gate was carved taller than the city temple's, and "precursor" fails because its festival was timed against a city festival already being held.

WIC27E-03.explanation: Young cod hide in crevices under the dark ice by day, and the seabirds that hunt by sight take most of the young cod only at the ice-free mouth of the bay, so the ice serves as the cod's "roof". "Pantry" fails because almost nothing grows under the thick, snowy ice and the cod swim out past its edge to feed. "Raft" fails because the ice is frozen fast to the shore and carries nothing, and "perch" fails because the cod live under the ice, not on it.

WIC27E-04.explanation: The river kept its usual flow, yet trout died by the thousands in the shallow, treeless lower miles while they lived in the shaded miles near the cold springs, so the drought "overheated" the river. "Pooled" fails because tagged trout traveled from the springs downstream. "Pinched" fails because the mill turned at its usual speed, and "parched" fails because the springs held up.

WIC27E-05.explanation: The town had shrunk to four hundred people with half its houses empty, miners rented those houses and many stayed to farm idle land, and by 1920 a school closed since 1885 had reopened with three teachers, so the rush "repopulated" the town. "Overran" fails because the miners filled houses already standing empty. "Ruined" fails because the reopened school shows a growing town, and "reoriented" fails because the new farmers shipped from the old river landing.

WIC27E-06.explanation: A dozen scattered pockets were each dug out in daylight into craters, some a quarter mile across, with old forest between them, so mining had "pitted" the mountain. "Riddled" fails because the miners worked from the surface, not through tunnels. "Razed" fails because the mountain still shades the town until nine, and "poisoned" fails because a trout hatchery still uses its water.

WIC27E-07.explanation: The duty rose under one party and fell under the other as they traded office, ending within a cent of where it began, so it was a "pendulum". "Ratchet" fails because the duty came back to its starting level. "Regulator" fails because two rises came in years of record prices, and "pacemaker" fails because the neighbors kept their 1850 duties throughout.

WIC27E-08.explanation: The doors were sealed until 1945, the reading rooms were used to store army files, and inside even the banned authors, the bound newspapers and the sealed rare-book room were untouched, so the occupation had "padlocked" the library. "Purged" fails because the banned authors still stood on the shelves. "Pulped" fails because the bound newspapers lay under five years of dust, and "plundered" fails because the rare-book room's seal of 1940 was unbroken.
